title: Best Free Browser Games With No Download (2026)
html:
The best browser games in 2026 look like console games and load in a tab. No installer, no launcher, no store page. Open a link and play.

The short answer: the Riftn Arcade puts ten free games in one place, from cinematic 3D chess to a side-scrolling brawler and Okey with friends. Every one runs in the browser, and none of them sells you anything. Below is each game, what it needs, and a few favourites from outside Riftn.

The 10 best free browser games on Riftn

1. King's Gambit: cinematic 3D chess

Chess with an army behind every piece. Three civilisations march, strike and fall across a marble board in four battlegrounds. Play the engine at three strengths, or play people online and climb a ladder rated on Elo. Prefer slow chess? Correspondence chess gives each move days, not seconds.

Play King's Gambit

2. Street Slayer: a neon street brawler

A side-scrolling beat 'em up, made for Riftn alone by Studio Shook Pixel. Pick one of three fighters, then punch, kick and throw your way down the block. A leaderboard ranks how far down the street you get.

Play Street Slayer

3. God's Eye: a live 3D globe

Spin a live 3D Earth with spatial-intelligence displays. If you choose, place a deliberately rough version of your location on it and find other Riftn members around the world.

Open God's Eye

4. Chartopia: a trading floor you can walk

Dozens of screens curve around a desk, carrying live feeds from Binance, Dexscreener, videos and browser tabs. Walk the floor in the browser, or enter it in a VR headset.

Take the desk in Chartopia

5. Claude of Duty: a browser shooter built from code

A first-person shooter that ships no art at all. Every mesh, texture, weapon and sound is generated on your machine while the level loads, so the first load takes up to a minute.

Play Claude of Duty

6. Jungle Trail: a rainforest walk

A first-person walk through a rainforest grown as you arrive: a hundred thousand plants, weather and a day cycle. No enemies, no timer. Just walk.

Walk Jungle Trail

7. Okey 101: the tile game, with friends

Four seats. Invite friends, and bots fill any empty seat. Open a public table or lock one with a password. Just for fun, no money.

Play Okey 101

8. Chestard: a retro arcade puzzle

Roll the die, drop the checker, clear the bottom row before the board tops out. A top 10 keeps score.

Play Chestard

9. SillyCoin: a tap-to-mine idle game

Tap to mine, buy upgrades and send coins to friends. The coins are just for fun and have no value.

Play SillyCoin

10. Gratitude pen pals: a two-player word game

Take turns naming something you are grateful for. No repeats. Miss your turn and the other player wins.

Play Gratitude pen pals

What you need to play

  • A recent browser: Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
  • Graphics acceleration for the 3D games: King's Gambit, God's Eye, Chartopia, Claude of Duty and Jungle Trail use WebGL. A laptop from the last few years handles them. Older phones may struggle.
  • Nothing else: no download, no plug-in and no payment. Sign in only to play with friends or put your name on a leaderboard.

More free browser games worth a tab

  • Lichess: free, open source chess with no ads.
  • Wordle: one five-letter word a day.
  • Krunker: a fast arena shooter in the browser.
  • Slither.io: the multiplayer snake game that never gets old.
  • Poki and CrazyGames: portals with thousands of casual browser games.

For game developers

The Riftn Arcade accepts submissions. Send your browser game from the Arcade page, and the team reviews each one before it is listed. Riftn is a social media protocol, so players can share clips and talk about your game in the same place they play it.

Frequently asked questions

What are the best free browser games with no download?

On Riftn: King's Gambit for 3D chess, Street Slayer for an arcade brawler, and Okey 101 to play with friends. Outside Riftn: Lichess, Wordle and Krunker.

Are Riftn Arcade games really free?

Yes. Every game is free to play, with no in-game purchases. SillyCoin's coins have no value.

Do I need an account to play?

No. Open a game and play. Sign in only to play friends online or to join a leaderboard.

Can I play on my phone?

Yes, in the phone's browser. The 2D games run on any phone. The 3D games need a recent phone with good graphics.

Can I play browser games at school or work?

Browser games need no install, so they run on most computers. Your school or employer's network rules still apply.
